initial_requirements: Philips Digital Systems Laboratories wants an instant-messaging application that demonstrates communication through its interactive television platform. Television users should sign in with an existing account, see which friends are online and what programs they are watching, exchange text messages, manage their presence and nickname, and maintain a buddy list. Users should also be able to block contacts and receive visible notifications when messages arrive.

turns.interviewer_utterance: Could you describe the core messaging and buddy-list capabilities the application must support, including any specific rules for presence updates, nickname management, blocking contacts, and message notifications?
turns.interviewee_utterance: The application needs to let a user send and receive plain text instant messages with people on their buddy list, and it should show which buddies are currently online and, when available, what program or channel they’re watching. Users should be able to add and remove buddies, see their presence status update in near real time, and change their own nickname so it’s reflected to others. If a contact is blocked, that person should no longer be able to message the user or appear as available in the normal buddy view, and incoming messages should trigger a clear visible on-screen notification so the user knows something has arrived even if they’re not actively in the chat.

turns.interviewer_utterance: When a recipient is offline or unavailable, should the system queue incoming messages for later delivery and keep message history available for viewing, and if so, how long should those messages and chat logs be retained?
turns.interviewee_utterance: Yes, I’d expect offline messages to be queued so they can be delivered when the recipient comes back online, as long as that fits the platform’s messaging model. I’m not sure we’ve decided the retention period yet for queued messages or chat history, so I’d need to check with the team on how long we want to keep them and whether users should be able to view older logs from the TV interface.

turns.interviewer_utterance: What retention and access rules should apply to message data: how long should queued offline messages and chat history be kept, when should queued messages expire if a recipient does not return online, and should users be able to view past chat history from the TV interface?
turns.interviewee_utterance: I don’t have a firm policy for the exact retention period yet, so that would need to be confirmed with the team. My expectation is that queued offline messages should not be kept indefinitely; they should expire after some reasonable window if the recipient never comes back online, and chat history should be limited rather than permanent for privacy and storage reasons. For the TV interface, I’d want at least recent conversation history available to view, but I can’t say yet whether we should support full past logs or only the current session until that’s decided.

turns.interviewer_utterance: What privacy controls should users have over their presence visibility and sharing of viewing activity—for example, should they be able to appear offline, hide what program or channel they’re watching, or limit that information to certain buddies or groups?
turns.interviewee_utterance: Yes, users should have some control over that. At minimum they should be able to appear offline if they want to, and they should be able to hide what they’re watching from other users. I’m not sure yet whether we want finer-grained controls like sharing that activity only with certain buddies or groups, so that would need to be verified.

slots.name: project_goals
slots.value: Provide an instant-messaging application for Philips interactive television that lets TV users communicate with buddies, view presence and viewing activity, and manage messaging identity and contact controls.

slots.name: stakeholder_roles
slots.value: TV users with existing accounts are the primary users; buddies/contacts are the messaging recipients; Philips Digital Systems Laboratories is the sponsoring stakeholder.

slots.name: functional_needs
slots.value: Users must be able to sign in with an existing account, send and receive plain text instant messages to people on their buddy list, view which buddies are online and what program/channel they are watching when available, add and remove buddies, see presence updates in near real time, change their nickname, block contacts, receive clear visible on-screen notifications for incoming messages, and have offline messages queued for delivery when recipients return online.

slots.name: business_rules
slots.value: Messaging is limited to plain text and primarily to people on the buddy list; blocked contacts must not be able to message the user and must not appear as available in the normal buddy view; a user's nickname changes must be reflected to others; presence should update near real time; offline messages should be queued until the recipient comes back online.

slots.name: data_entities
slots.value: User account, buddy list/contact list, buddy presence status, viewing activity (program or channel), nickname, blocked contacts, instant messages, queued offline messages, and chat history/logs.

slots.name: constraints
slots.value: The application runs on Philips's interactive television platform and uses existing user accounts; communication is restricted to plain text instant messaging.

slots.name: quality_concerns
slots.value: Presence updates should be near real time, incoming messages must produce a clear visible on-screen notification so users notice them even when not actively in chat, and offline messages should be delivered when recipients reconnect.

slots.name: boundary_conditions
slots.value: If a contact is blocked, that contact cannot send messages to the user and should not appear as available in the normal buddy view; viewing program/channel information is only shown when available; offline messages are queued for later delivery when recipients are unavailable.

slots.name: message_history_retention
slots.value: Chat history retention is not yet decided; the stakeholder wants it limited rather than permanent, with at least recent conversation history available on the TV interface.

slots.name: offline_message_handling
slots.value: Offline messages should be queued while the recipient is unavailable and delivered when the recipient comes back online.

slots.name: notification_display_behavior
slots.value: Incoming messages should trigger a clear, visible on-screen notification so the user notices new messages even when not actively in chat.

slots.name: account_authentication_flow
slots.value: Users sign in with an existing account.

slots.name: presence_privacy_controls
slots.value: Users should be able to appear offline if they want to.

slots.name: chat_history_accessibility
slots.value: At least recent conversation history should be viewable from the TV interface, but full past-log access is not yet decided.

slots.name: message_retention_period
slots.value: The exact retention period is not yet confirmed; queued offline messages and chat history should be kept only for a limited, reasonable period rather than permanently.

slots.name: queued_message_expiration
slots.value: Queued offline messages should expire after a reasonable window if the recipient does not come back online, but the exact expiration time is not yet defined.

slots.name: presence_visibility_settings
slots.value: Users should be able to hide their presence status and appear offline.

slots.name: viewing_activity_sharing_controls
slots.value: Users should be able to hide what program or channel they are watching from other users; finer-grained sharing rules are not yet decided.

slots.name: buddy_presence_audience_rules
slots.value: Presence and viewing activity are generally visible to other users in the buddy view, but users may hide their presence or viewing activity; finer-grained audience controls are not yet decided.

abduction_history.surprising_fact: The stakeholder expects the IM app to use existing accounts on an interactive TV platform, but the exact visibility of online status and viewing activity is still implied to be limited by privacy concerns, suggesting presence may need finer-grained user control than initially described.
abduction_history.suspected_reason: Because the service exposes not only online status but also what program or channel a buddy is watching, the team likely needs privacy-preserving presence controls so users can avoid over-disclosing activity while still supporting social awareness on TV.
